text:
jordan (AcmeCI): Hey team — we just hit our monthly refill window and the credits showed up in the console, but within ~30s they dropped to 0. We have background ingestion workers that run at midnight local time; they were supposed to start after refill. Can you confirm how the refill timing works and if there's any protection against immediate burst consumption? Account: acme-123. Logs below.

alex: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact timestamps (UTC) when you saw the refill and when usage dropped? Also, are the ingestion workers using the same API key or multiple keys?

jordan (AcmeCI): Refill event in console: "2026-02-01T00:00:02Z" (screenshot). Usage spike shows first request 2026-02-01T00:00:05Z and by 00:00:35Z balance 0. Workers use 10 parallel clients with the same org key. We expected refill to be effective for jobs scheduled at midnight local (America/Los_Angeles).

maria: Two things to confirm: (1) which timezone the org billing window is configured for (some older accounts had per-org TZ), (2) whether you have any reserved capacity or dedicated pools that might be billed differently.

support-bot: Automated note: monthly credits are scheduled to allocate on the first day of the billing period at 00:00:00 UTC by default. If your account has a custom billing timezone, allocation occurs at 00:00:00 in that timezone.

alex: Based on the timestamps you pasted it looks like the refill occurred at 00:00:02Z and requests started at 00:00:05Z — so refill had already occurred. That suggests the burst consumption came from queued/parallel workers all firing at once. Can you share a short excerpt of the ingestion client logs (requests per second around that time)?

jordan (AcmeCI): Paste of condensed logs (redacted):

```
2026-02-01T00:00:03Z Worker-01 POST /v1/generate  tokens_used=1200
2026-02-01T00:00:03Z Worker-02 POST /v1/generate  tokens_used=1100
2026-02-01T00:00:04Z Worker-03 POST /v1/generate  tokens_used=1300
2026-02-01T00:00:05Z Worker-04 POST /v1/generate  tokens_used=1400
2026-02-01T00:00:06Z Worker-05 POST /v1/generate  tokens_used=1500
-- total ~6500 tokens in 3s, then responded 429 / balance=0
```

alex: That matches a parallel burst that could exhaust a freshly-refilled quota. When multiple clients hit at once you can see a race where many requests are allowed concurrently before the central balance reflects the depletion. We have soft-rate limiting on the billing side but there can be a short window.

lee (billing-engineer): Hi Jordan — I pulled the billing ledger for acme-123. Refill was applied at 2026-02-01T00:00:02Z UTC for 50,000 credits. All usage records for the spike were accepted and consumed. We do have eventual consistency (sub-second) for the balance view; however, high parallelism can cause many requests to be accepted before every client has the up-to-date remaining balance.

lee (billing-engineer): Quick answers:
- Refill timing: default 00:00 UTC. Some legacy orgs can be configured for a non-UTC tz (we can confirm if you'd like).
- No rollover: unused monthly credits do NOT carry over unless you are on an explicit rollover plan.
- Immediate exhaustion protection: we don't block heavy parallel bursts immediately on refill; we recommend application-side throttles.

maria: For troubleshooting / repro: could you temporarily run a short test that sequentially issues 1 request every 250ms starting at midnight and report back whether the balance holds? That will help differentiate race acceptance vs. actual higher token counts per call.

jordan (AcmeCI): We ran an isolated test: 1 req / 250ms starting at 00:00:02Z. Balance decreased as expected, no 429s. The problem seems to be the fan-out of all 10 workers starting within the same second.

sre-oncall: Filed INC-4321: "reprorate: high concurrency acceptance window causes refill -> burst exhaustion". Short-term mitigation suggested below.

alex: Suggested mitigations:
- Stagger worker start times by a few seconds (random jitter) so they don't all fire on the exact second.
- Check client-side token budgeting: each worker should check available balance API before starting large batches.
- Use rate_limit headers from the API and implement exponential backoff on 429s.
- Use the Console's "soft quota" or per-key caps (support can set temporary per-key limits).

lee (billing-engineer): We can offer a one-time emergency credit top-up while you roll out staggers. If you'd like, we can also set a soft per-key cap for the next cycle to prevent rebuild of the same pattern.

jordan (AcmeCI): Yes please on the temporary top-up and also would like to set a per-key cap of 10k tokens for the next 24h. Also please confirm whether our org has custom timezone billing (we're a legacy account).

lee (billing-engineer): Done: added +20,000 one-time credit at 2026-02-01T00:05:30Z (visible in ledger). Set per-key soft cap 10,000 tokens for 24h. Billing window for acme-123: legacy TZ = America/Los_Angeles; next scheduled refill is 2026-03-01T00:00:00-08:00 (which is 2026-03-01T08:00:00Z). I've added a note to your org profile that refill timezone is PDT.

maria: Next steps for you (short list):
- Roll out jittered worker starts (we can provide a small client-side library snippet)
- Implement per-key pre-flight balance check before large batches
- Optionally enable per-key soft caps via Support ahead of next cycle

alex: Client-side snippet suggestion (very small):
```
// simple jittered start
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 5000); // ms
setTimeout(() => startWorker(), jitter);

async function startWorker(){
  const bal = await fetch('/v1/orgs/me/credits');
  if (bal.remaining < expectedBatch) return; // skip or wait
  // proceed
}
```

jordan (AcmeCI): That helps a lot, thanks. One more question — is there any plan to make the refill+consumption window atomic so a refilled balance can't be drained by bursts in the first few seconds?

lee (billing-engineer): There's an internal discussion. Long-term we'd like stronger enforcement (token reservation) at allocation time for known scheduled jobs, but that needs changes to how we accept distributed requests. For now the recommended pattern is application-side smoothing + soft caps. We logged feature request FEAT-211 for stronger allocation semantics.

sre-oncall: Closing note: incident created and triaged. Engineering will evaluate a server-side throttling change; target initial design doc due in 2 sprints.

jordan (AcmeCI): OK thanks everyone — the top-up and caps fixed our immediate outage. We'll implement jitter and pre-flight checks for future cycles. :thumbsup:

alex: Glad this helped. If you want, we can pair for 20min to add the jitter to your deploy pipeline.

support-bot: Thread resolved by support. If anything recurs, reopen and tag @sre-oncall or @lee.
